projects.title: Immunization app
projects.description:
Programmers: Roberto Chupin, Christopher Cruz, James Bates, Sam Messina, and Jason Zoller
Graphic Designers: Alina Nusrat and Candice Loud

Vaccination records are necessary for the welfare of children and adults. Unfortunately, third world countries are having trouble keeping up-to-date information on their patient’s vaccination records. In some cases, records are not accurately filled out because they are designed in a complex manner, which can lead to patients getting too much of a certain vaccination. Records need to be correct so that they maintain an accurate health history for the patient. If records are confusing, redundant, or inaccessible, it becomes harder for medical personnel to provide life-saving vaccines to patients. Our mission is to revolutionize medical record keeping by developing an application that enhances the synergistic relationship between healthcare professionals and pediatric patients, while keeping in mind the confidentiality of the patient’s information. Our application is designed for the iPad to make it easier for doctors to use, and portable to any area that has Internet. Additionally, it will help doctors securely login, search for patient’s records, and edit minor details of the patient’s information. Only the administrator will be allowed to make major changes to the patient’s information. Moreover, the database will provide data validation and protection. Hence, technology has opened- up so many possibilities to progress health care. Thus, we have made it our goal to create an innovative way to optimize the portability, accuracy, security, and accessibility for doctors to gain access to the vaccination records as quickly as possible.

projects.title: FLL Scoring Application
projects.description: Scoring application I developed on a team of 2 for a First Lego League chapter. The purpose of the application was to simplify scoring and judging for competitions, while having a secure site for judges and administrators. Technology used was ruby on rails, with a  PostgreSQL database, bootstrap, and javascript.
